name: Nisshi
description: Nisshi (formerly Tansu) is a stateless, Apache Kafka compatible broker with pluggable storage. This script installs the single binary with the embedded SQLite storage engine and can optionally point it at your own S3 bucket or PostgreSQL database for storage, an Apache Iceberg REST catalog for lakehouse tables and an OpenTelemetry collector for metrics.

app_vars.name: var_nisshi_storage
app_vars.label: Storage Engine
app_vars.help: sqlite keeps everything in /var/lib/nisshi/nisshi.db. s3 and postgres use a service you already run - nothing besides Nisshi is installed in the container.

app_vars.name: var_nisshi_postgres_url
app_vars.label: PostgreSQL URL
app_vars.help: Only for the postgres storage engine, as postgres://user:password@host/database. Percent-encode special characters in the password. The Nisshi schema is loaded into this database during the install, so it must be reachable from the container.

app_vars.name: var_nisshi_s3_bucket
app_vars.label: S3 Storage Bucket
app_vars.help: Only for the s3 storage engine. The bucket must already exist.

app_vars.name: var_nisshi_s3_endpoint
app_vars.label: S3 Endpoint
app_vars.help: URL of your MinIO or other S3 compatible service, e.g. http://192.168.1.10:9000. Leave empty for AWS.

app_vars.name: var_nisshi_s3_access_key
app_vars.label: S3 Access Key ID
app_vars.help: Used for the s3 storage engine and for a data lake on s3://.

app_vars.name: var_nisshi_iceberg_catalog
app_vars.label: Iceberg REST Catalog URL
app_vars.help: e.g. http://192.168.1.11:8181/catalog for Lakekeeper. When set, topics that have a schema are also written as Apache Iceberg tables. Leave empty to run without a lakehouse.

app_vars.name: var_nisshi_lake_location
app_vars.label: Data Lake Location
app_vars.help: Where the Parquet files of the Iceberg tables are written, s3://lake/ when left empty. Only used with an Iceberg catalog.

app_vars.name: var_nisshi_iceberg_warehouse
app_vars.label: Iceberg Warehouse
app_vars.help: Warehouse name in the Iceberg catalog, if it needs one.

app_vars.name: var_nisshi_otlp_endpoint
app_vars.label: OTLP Metrics Endpoint
app_vars.help: OTLP/HTTP URL of your OpenTelemetry collector, e.g. http://192.168.1.12:4318. Leave empty to disable metrics export.

app_vars.name: var_nisshi_otlp_headers
app_vars.label: OTLP Headers
app_vars.help: Collector credentials as key=value pairs, e.g. Authorization=Bearer <token>.

notes.text: There is no web interface. Kafka clients connect to the container on port 9092.

The broker advertises the container IP it had during the install. If that IP changes, update ADVERTISED_LISTENER_URL in /opt/nisshi/.env and run systemctl restart nisshi, otherwise clients cannot connect.
No authentication or TLS is configured: anyone who can reach port 9092 can read and write topics.

With the default SQLite storage engine all data is in /var/lib/nisshi/nisshi.db. External S3, PostgreSQL, Iceberg and OpenTelemetry services are not installed by this script - it only stores their URLs and credentials in /opt/nisshi/.env.

The broker does not create its tables on PostgreSQL. Only when the postgres storage engine is chosen, the script installs postgresql-client and loads /opt/nisshi/etc/initdb.d/010-schema.sql into your database once. SQLite and S3 installs get no extra packages.

To add a lakehouse after the install, set SCHEMA_REGISTRY, DATA_LAKE and ICEBERG_CATALOG in /opt/nisshi/.env and change ExecStart in /etc/systemd/system/nisshi.service to end in 'broker iceberg', then run systemctl daemon-reload and systemctl restart nisshi.
With an Iceberg catalog configured, put the Avro, JSON or Protobuf schema of each topic into /var/lib/nisshi/schema. Only topics with a schema are written to the lakehouse.
